title: myCHEF vs CateringDubai.ae: which is better in 2026
body_markdown:
**Choose myCHEF if you want a vetted chef and a menu designed around your guest count, kitchen and dietary needs; choose CateringDubai.ae if its published menus and service format already match your event and you want to compare it against a fixed offer.** That is the real axis of difference in 2026: a service built around the client versus a service you assess against what it already lists.

This guide compares the two on process, menus, halal standards, staffing, pricing models and fit. For a wider field, see these [CateringDubai.ae alternatives](https://www.mychef.ae/blog/cateringdubai-ae-alternatives-in).


**TL;DR**

- myCHEF suits hosts who want a vetted chef and a menu designed around their event, home and guests.
- CateringDubai.ae suits buyers who prefer to judge a ready-made catering offer before committing.
- myCHEF vs CateringDubai.ae comes down to custom design versus choosing from what is listed.
- Compare written quotes on inclusions, staffing and cleanup, not on headline numbers alone.
- Verify every CateringDubai.ae detail directly with that company before you book in 2026.


## Why this comparison matters in 2026

Most Dubai hosts compare caterers on price first and discover the gaps later: who serves, who clears, who handles allergies, who is accountable if a guest count changes. A comparison that starts with those questions saves a bad evening.

myCHEF is a private chef and catering service in Dubai. It provides vetted chefs for home-cooked meals, weekly meal prep, dinner parties, corporate events and large catered celebrations. CateringDubai.ae is a separate company. This page does not state its prices, menus or policies, because those are not verified here. Where the comparison needs a CateringDubai.ae fact, it tells you what to ask for instead.

## At a glance

| Dimension | myCHEF | CateringDubai.ae |
|---|---|---|
| Best for | Hosts who want a chef and a menu designed around them | Buyers who want to assess a ready-made catering offer |
| Service model | Vetted chefs for home cooking, meal prep, dinner parties, corporate events and celebrations | Confirm directly with the company |
| Menu approach | Menu design built around guest count and dietary needs | Check its published menus against your brief |
| Halal approach | Halal-first standards | Ask for its halal sourcing and handling in writing |
| Chef vetting | Chefs are vetted and scored before they cook | Ask how its kitchen staff are selected |
| Pricing model | Quoted from your date, guests and service | Ask for a written itemised quote |
| Cleanup | Kitchen left exactly as found | Ask what the quote includes |
| Standout feature | One service from a weekly meal prep to a large celebration | Confirm directly with the company |

## myCHEF is built around the client

The core difference is the starting point. With myCHEF, you describe the occasion, the date, the location, the guest count and the service you need. The menu is designed from that brief.

That suits events where the food is the centrepiece: a dinner party at home, a birthday where guests have different dietary needs, a corporate lunch with a mixed group. The trade-off is honest. A designed service starts with a conversation, so you do not get a menu-to-cart experience on day one.

CateringDubai.ae may suit you better if you already know what you want and prefer to choose from something listed. Check its current menus on its own site rather than relying on a third-party summary.

## Chef vetting: myCHEF is clearer on process

myCHEF chefs are vetted and scored before they cook in a client's kitchen. For a home booking, that matters more than a polished menu, because a stranger is working in your kitchen.

For CateringDubai.ae, the useful question is plain: how are the people who cook and serve at your event selected and supervised? A good company answers that in one paragraph. If the answer is vague, treat it as information.

## Halal standards: ask both companies the same questions

myCHEF works halal-first. For many UAE households and corporate clients, halal is not a preference but a requirement, so the standard needs to be stated up front and not discovered at the tasting.

Whatever you choose, ask for the same four things in writing:

- How halal sourcing is handled for meat and poultry.
- Whether alcohol is used in any sauce, marinade or dessert.
- How cross-contact is managed for guests with allergies.
- Who is responsible on the day if a guest raises a dietary issue.

For a wider view of the market, see this guide to [halal catering companies in Dubai](https://www.mychef.ae/blog/best-halal-catering-companies-in-dubai).

## Staffing and cleanup: compare quotes line by line

This is where two similar-looking quotes diverge. One may include serving staff and cleanup; the other may price them separately or not at all. myCHEF's standard is a kitchen left exactly as we found it, and a quote should say what staffing is included for your format.

Ask CateringDubai.ae the same thing. How many staff attend, who serves, who clears, who removes equipment and waste, and what happens if your event runs late? The guide on [serving staff and cleanup from Dubai caterers](https://www.mychef.ae/blog/can-catering-companies-in-dubai-provide-serving-staff-and-cleanup) lists what to look for in a quote.

## Menu flexibility: myCHEF is the better fit for custom briefs

myCHEF designs the menu around the occasion, so changes for allergies, children, fasting guests or a specific cuisine are part of the process rather than an exception.

A fixed offer has its own strength: it is easier to judge. You see the dishes, you compare them and you decide. If your event is simple and your guests are not particular, that can be the faster route. Both approaches work. They solve different problems.

## Range of services: myCHEF covers more formats under one roof

myCHEF covers recurring and one-off needs: home-cooked meals, weekly meal prep, dinner parties, corporate events and large celebrations. That helps if you start with a single dinner and later want a weekly arrangement, because the chef relationship and your dietary notes carry over.

If you only need one catered event and never a chef again, that breadth has no value to you. Say so, and judge both companies purely on that one event.

## Pricing: compare the models, not the headline

This page does not publish a price for either company. Prices change, and only a written quote tells you what you will pay for your date and guest count.

The two models carry different trade-offs:

- **Quoted from your brief:** the price reflects your guest count, menu and service format. It is tailored, but you need the quote before you can compare.
- **Priced from a listed offer:** easier to compare early, but check what the listed price excludes.

Whichever you receive, line up the same items: food, chef or kitchen staff, serving staff, equipment, delivery or travel, cleanup and any minimum order. A quote that is cheaper on food and silent on cleanup is not cheaper.

## Scorecard

| Dimension | Better fit |
|---|---|
| Custom menu design | myCHEF |
| Chef vetting process | myCHEF |
| Halal-first approach | myCHEF |
| Cleanup standard | myCHEF |
| Judging a listed offer at a glance | CateringDubai.ae, if its menus match your event |
| Simple one-off event with a fixed menu | Tie, depending on the quote |
| Price | Tie until you hold two written quotes |

Two of those rows are honest ties. Without verified CateringDubai.ae data, a clean sweep would be invented, and you should not trust a comparison that gives you one.

## A five-question checklist before you book either

1. Who exactly cooks and serves at my event, and how were they selected?
2. What is included: staff, equipment, setup and cleanup?
3. How are halal and allergy requirements handled and confirmed in writing?
4. What happens if my guest count changes close to the date?
5. Who is my single point of contact on the day?

If a company answers all five clearly before you pay a deposit, it is a serious option. If it cannot, move on.

## Choose myCHEF if

- You are hosting at home or on a property where a chef will work in your kitchen.
- You want the menu designed around your guests, not selected from a list.
- Halal-first handling and vetted chefs are requirements, not bonuses.
- You may want weekly meal prep or repeat dinners later.

## Choose CateringDubai.ae if

- Its published menus and format already match your event closely.
- You prefer to evaluate a ready-made offer before speaking to anyone.
- Its written quote covers staffing, equipment and cleanup at a price that suits your budget.

For a broader shortlist, the guide to the [best catering companies in Dubai](https://www.mychef.ae/blog/best-catering-companies-in-dubai) covers more options.

**Does myCHEF clean up after cooking?**

Yes. The standard is a kitchen left exactly as we found it. Confirm the arrangement for your format when you receive the quote.

**How do I compare caterer quotes in Dubai?**

Line up the same items in each quote: food, chef or kitchen staff, serving staff, equipment, delivery and cleanup. A lower food price means little if staffing or cleanup is excluded.

**What does myCHEF need to prepare a quote?**

Your date, location, guest count and the service you want. Dietary needs and cuisine preferences help shape the menu.

**Can I verify CateringDubai.ae details through myCHEF?**

No. CateringDubai.ae is a separate company, so confirm its menus, prices and policies directly with it before you book.

Yes. myCHEF provides home-cooked meals, weekly meal prep, dinner parties, corporate events and large celebrations.
